title: Zakariyya's quiet prayer
hookLine: an old man with gray hair and no children prays in a whisper, and is given a son named Yahya
tomorrow: the messenger in the eastern place

lines: AN OLD MAN IN THE ROOM OF PRAYER.
cards: Stay in that little room a minute longer. Zakariyya has just heard the girl in his care say that the food came from Allah, who gives without counting. And something stirs in him.
He's old. His bones are weak, his hair has gone white, and his wife has never been able to have children. For years that door has been closed, and he's stopped knocking.
And right there, the Qur'an says, he prayed. Not loudly. Not in front of anyone.
The nineteenth surah, named for Maryam, opens with exactly this: an old man, alone, whispering.

teach.b: In Pickthall's translation of Surah Maryam: “When he cried unto his Lord a cry in secret.” In Arabic, nida'an khafiyya. A call, a hidden one.
Why secret? Commentators offered a few reasons. A quiet prayer is closer to sincerity: no one to impress.
Or maybe he felt a little shy, asking for a baby at his age. Listen to how he makes his case.

teach.h: MY HEAD IS SHINING WITH GRAY HAIR.
teach.b: My bones are weak, he says, and my head is shining with gray hair.

teach.h: NEVER UNBLEST IN PRAYER TO THEE.
teach.b: Then the line that holds the whole prayer together: “I have never been unblest in prayer to Thee, my Lord.” Every time I've asked, You've been good to me. That's his reason for hoping.
Not his strength, not his record. Just a lifetime of being answered. He asks for an heir, someone to carry on the family of Ya'qub, someone pleasing to Allah.

teach.h: A SON NAMED YAHYA, AND A SILENCE.
teach.b: The answer comes, through angels, while he's standing in prayer: good news of a son, and his name is Yahya. The Qur'an says no one had been given that name before. Zakariyya is astonished.
How, when I'm this old and my wife is barren?

He's told: it is easy for your Lord. Then he asks for a sign, and the sign is silence: for three nights he won't be able to speak to people, though he's well. The man who prayed in a whisper is given days of quiet.
Christians know this child too, as John the Baptist.
And that closes week ten: bid', truthful one, a heart that doesn't clear itself, brothers at the gate, forgive one old thing, out loud, fruit without measure, and a whisper that was heard.

how: Muslims make du'a aloud and in private; Zakariyya's prayer for a child, in Surah Maryam, Surah Al 'Imran and Surah Al-Anbiya (21:89), is one that couples hoping for a child sometimes recite.

games.q: Zakariyya is old, his wife has never had children, and he has just seen food in Maryam's room that no one brought. what does he do?
o: announce to everyone that a miracle is coming.
games.why: right there he prayed (3:38), a cry in secret (19:3). the answer: a son named Yahya.

practice: Think of one thing you've quietly given up on: a hope you stopped mentioning, a person you stopped expecting to change, a door you stopped knocking on. Don't argue with it; just name it, inside.
If you pray, you can ask for it again, quietly, the way Zakariyya did; if you don't, just let yourself hope for it for two minutes, without defending the hope.
